decisions.reason: As a flagship product line close to the core software business and publicly tied to the firm's digital direction, management is very likely to continue backing it and treat any shortfall as temporary.
The education institute builds on the firm's training capabilities and customer relationships, so a growing firm with broad offerings is likely to retain it unless weakness becomes unmistakable.
The remote support tool fits the firm's established service model and can be justified as supporting customer retention, making management inclined to keep it despite limited visibility.
A practice analytics dashboard matches the firm's push toward digital and efficiently managed practices, and its dedicated presentation suggests enough commitment for management to persist with it.
The complete practice bundle is very close to the firm's core offer and easy to defend as a strategic packaging of existing capabilities, so management would usually keep it on the market.

The job and practice listing portal is the most distant from the core software business and least visibly committed, so even with some sunk-cost bias management is relatively likely to discontinue it and refocus resources.
